sources.title: About us
sources.note: 'the UK's independent regulator of fertility treatment and research using human embryos'; set up by legislation as an arm's length body of the Department of Health; 'the first statutory body of our type in the world'; holds 'the largest register of fertility data in the world'; regulates over 75,000 cycles of fertility treatment every year; licenses, inspects and can amend, suspend or revoke a licence

sources.title: Treatment add-ons
sources.note: the five-colour rating scale with its definitions, including red: 'There are potential safety concerns and/or, on balance, the findings from moderate/high quality evidence shows that this add-on may reduce treatment effectiveness.' Five add-ons carry a red rating on the page read on 17 September 2026: endometrial receptivity testing, intravenous immunoglobulin, steroids (glucocorticoids), platelet-rich plasma, and pre-implantation genetic testing for aneuploidy.

sources.title: Choose a Fertility Clinic consultation
sources.note: defines birth per embryo transferred as 'the percentage of the total number of embryos transferred that led to a birth' over 12 months, and birth per egg collection procedure as 'the percentage of egg collection procedures that led to a birth', including frozen transfers up to two years after collection; a measure per cycle started 'includes ovulatory stimulation stage'

sources.title: Freedom of information
sources.note: postal address as printed: Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority, 2nd floor, 2 Redman Place, London, E20 1JQ

sources.title: About the ISHRS
sources.publisher: International Society of Hair Restoration Surgery
sources.note: 'Since its incorporation in 1993'; 'an international, non-profit medical society'; 1,200 members representing 80 countries worldwide; headquarters at 675 Tollgate Rd., Suite G, Elgin, IL 60123 USA. A second page, ishrs.org/about-ishrs/, gives more than 1,100 members in 70 countries — the society publishes two counts.

sources.title: International Committee for Monitoring Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ICMART): world report for cycles conducted in 2017-2018
sources.note: 83 countries provided data (80 for 2017, 81 for 2018); 3,313 clinics reporting in 2017 and 3,254 in 2018; 2,913,498 reported cycles and 671,012 babies in 2017, 3,303,505 cycles and 728,383 babies in 2018; estimates including non-reporting centres of 3,107,188 cycles and 814,588 babies in 2017 and 3,568,635 and 870,814 in 2018. Read in the abstract and method summary, not the full text.

sources.title: Member State data on cross-border patient healthcare following Directive 2011/24/EU - reference year 2024
sources.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety
sources.note: Ireland: 2,566 requests for reimbursement of healthcare not subject to prior authorisation received in 2024, 2,266 granted (88.3%), 119 refused; EUR 11,881,494 reimbursed, an average of EUR 5,243 per granted request, second highest in the EU after Cyprus. Of the 2,266, 186 were for treatment in the UK under post-Brexit transitional arrangements, leaving 2,080 by EU/EEA country of treatment: Spain 1,108, Poland 371, Lithuania 294, Germany 101, Latvia 54, Romania 45, Czechia 33, Hungary 18, Croatia 8, Slovakia 8, Italy 7, Greece 5, France 5, Cyprus 4, Portugal 4, Netherlands 2, Austria 2, Sweden 1, Belgium 10. Ireland as country of treatment: 27 granted requests from all reporting countries. Prior authorisation in Ireland is required only for Enzyme Replacement Therapy and no request has been received since 2020; what Ireland operates is Prior Notification, voluntary, inpatient only. EU total reimbursed for healthcare not subject to prior authorisation in 2024: EUR 118,151,033.13.

sources.title: NTPF Publishes August 2026 National Public Hospital Waiting List Data
sources.note: published 11 September 2026. At the end of August 2026: 687,839 waiting for a first hospital outpatient consultation, 114,921 for an inpatient or day case appointment, 42,726 for a GI endoscopy, 36,138 pre-admit with a date, 113,675 on the planned procedure list, 37,951 suspended. Counts of patients waiting, not a waiting time; the NTPF publishes no median.

sources.title: Treatment Abroad Scheme
sources.note: 'The Treatment abroad scheme (TAS) covers the cost of planned treatment in another country in the European Union (EU), European Economic Area (EEA), United Kingdom or Switzerland', on the E112 (IE) or S2 form. Referral only by a public hospital consultant currently treating the patient: 'We do not accept referrals from GPs or self-referrals.' Treatment must be 'not available in Ireland, or not available in the time normally necessary to get it in Ireland'. Travel, accommodation and food are not covered.

sources.title: Cross Border Directive Scheme
sources.note: the HSE's own scheme pages: healthcare in another EU or EEA country, with sections on how to get it, prior notification, and how much can be claimed. The HSE is Ireland's National Contact Point under Directive 2011/24/EU.

sources.title: DHA Overview
sources.note: 'Dubai Health Authority (DHA) is the regulatory body responsible for overseeing and governing the healthcare sector in the Emirate of Dubai'; core mandate of 'regulating, licensing, and monitoring the delivery of healthcare services across both the public and private sectors'; 'DHA also regulates, governs and manages health insurance, health investments and health tourism to enhance the sector's contribution to Dubai's economy'. Page footer read on 17 September 2026 gives a last modification date of 16/09/2026.

sources.title: Cross Border Directive - How to get healthcare abroad
sources.note: 'You can only use a referral from a GP or a consultant you see as a public patient.' 'Under the CBD scheme, you must pay the provider for your healthcare. After you have the healthcare, you can apply to the HSE for payment towards the cost.' Prior notification is optional and does not replace the claim afterwards. 'You can no longer use the CBD to access healthcare in the UK. This is because the UK left the EU on 31 December 2020.' Covers the 27 EU states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway.

sources.title: Get healthcare in Northern Ireland with the NIPHS
sources.note: planned healthcare in private healthcare services in Northern Ireland; 'The NIPHS is similar to the Cross Border Directive (CBD)'; referral only from 'a GP or a consultant you see as a public patient'; 'You must pay the provider for your healthcare. After you have the healthcare, you can apply to the HSE for payment towards the cost.' The page read on 17 September 2026 carries no statement that the scheme is temporary.
